canonicalFindings.title: emergencyWithdraw decrements totalStaked without recomputing the reward schedule, over-emitting to remaining stakers (reward-budget value leak)
canonicalFindings.severityDispute: Medium<->High (econ-scanner). Tier-3 SOLVENCY invariant PASSED => value-leak, not insolvency; pure value-leak/grief leg is permissionless but self-profit leg needs stated assumptions (recoverable capital + side position + inactivity window). FLAG for severity-classifier to resolve; preserve High note per conflicting-severity rule.
canonicalFindings.humanReviewFlag: severity (Medium vs High) — confirmed-live with PoC, label is the only open question
canonicalFindings.rootCause: NFTStaker.emergencyWithdraw reduces totalStaked but calls neither _updatePool nor _recomputeSchedule, so rewardRate stays sized for the pre-withdrawal (larger) pool. The next _updatePool then over-emits to the remaining stakers by oldTotal/newTotal, draining rewardBudget faster than targetAPY permits and reintroducing the per-participant multiplier that M-03 was meant to eliminate (APY-AS-FLOOR invariant breach).

locations.role: the recompute that emergencyWithdraw fails to call

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: emergencyWithdraw (src/NFTStaker.sol:538-561, esp. line 545) decrements totalStaked on principal return but does not re-settle or re-size the emission schedule: it skips both _updatePool and _recomputeSchedule. rewardRate is therefore left sized for the old, larger pool. On the next _updatePool, the unchanged rate is divided across a smaller totalStaked, so each remaining staker accrues at an inflated per-share rate (PoC measured ~100x), draining rewardBudget faster than the targetAPY policy allows. This re-introduces the participation multiplier that M-03 (APY-AS-FLOOR) was designed to remove. A self-profit variant exists where an attacker stakes, runs a side position to benefit from the inflated rate during an inactivity window, then recovers principal via emergencyWithdraw. Impact is value leak / mis-emission of the reward budget, not insolvency.

evidence.strongest: Tier-3 invariant PoC: workspace/phoenix-nft-staking/test/Invariant.t.sol — deterministic test FAILED and fuzz invariant FAILED, shrunk to the sequence stake -> emergencyWithdraw; SOLVENCY invariant (balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt) PASSED (=> value-leak classification, not insolvency).

canonicalFindings.relatedInvariant: profiles INDEX NFTStaker #4 APY-AS-FLOOR (M-03) and #3 RATE-FORMULA/RUNWAY — both violated by the missing recompute
canonicalFindings.consolidationNote: Single-source root cause; no duplicates to merge. Distinct from H-01/M-01 (BatchNFTMinter nudge) and from the NFTStaker reentrancy tool-cluster (a real accounting bug, not a tool pattern). Not present in the ledger — genuinely NEW.

canonicalFindings.title: Winner-take-all nudge pot: full balance-based payout on a count-only gate is permissionlessly front-runnable and silently over-fundable
canonicalFindings.rootCause: batchMint pays the FULL nudgePaymentToken balance to a caller-chosen recipient on a purely count-based gate (count >= nudgeSize), decoupled from the value the caller contributed. A searcher can copy a qualifying batch with recipient=self and a higher gas bid and scoop the whole externally-funded pot; the minReward floor (story-015) only protects the loser, not the pot. The same value-blind design is also a non-obvious owner over-funding footgun (Law 3).

locations.role: full-pot snapshot + count-only gate + caller-chosen-recipient payout

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: The nudge reads nudgeAmount = balanceOf(nudgePaymentToken) (full pot) and transfers it to a caller-chosen recipient whenever count >= nudgeSize, with no relation between the payout and the value the caller paid. This is a permissionless winner-take-all pot: a searcher who sees a qualifying batchMint in the mempool copies it with recipient=self and a higher gas bid, pays for the same nudgeSize real mints, and takes the entire pot. story-015's minReward floor only lets the LOSER bail on a sniped (now-zero) reward; the winner still takes the whole balance-based payout. story-016's snapshot-before-loop closes the donation-self-refund sub-vector but not the race. RE-EXAMINATION (this run): the acknowledged operational mitigation 'keep pot < nudgeSize x mintPrice' does NOT bound the loss, because each loop iteration mints a REAL, potentially resellable/redeemable NFT to recipient — a searcher who can realize NFT value nets ~pot > 0 for ANY pot size, so the giveaway is raced to zero on every refill. The owner over-funding facet (PATTERN-002, Law-3 footgun) folds in here: 'fund the incentive' silently equals 'set a sweepable bounty'.

evidence.strongest: Existing validated PoC workspace/phoenix-nft-staking/test/poc-MevFrontrunNudge.t.sol (ledger M-01); re-confirmed present at HEAD 5f863d2 by PATTERN-001 + econ/story re-examination.

canonicalFindings.title: batchMint lacks nonReentrant while custodying the nudge pot and using balance-based accounting across an ERC1155-callback mint loop
canonicalFindings.rootCause: BatchNFTMinter.batchMint is whenNotPaused but NOT nonReentrant (ReentrancyGuard is imported only by NFTStaker), yet it does balance-based pot accounting across a count-length loop of nftMinter.mint() calls, each of which fires the caller-chosen recipient's onERC1155Received. Defense-in-depth gap.

locations.role: unguarded fund-moving entrypoint with mid-loop ERC1155 callback

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: batchMint has no reentrancy guard while it is the only fund-moving entrypoint: it pulls payment, forceApproves the minter, runs a count-length loop of nftMinter.mint() (each dispatching an ERC1155 mint whose onERC1155Received runs the caller-chosen recipient's code), then transfers the balance-snapshotted nudge pot and refunds dust. Because accounting is contract-balance-based rather than per-call escrow, a guard is warranted for defense-in-depth. Tier-2 traced every reentry path and CONFIRMED NOT exploitable for theft: re-entry only fires into the attacker's own chosen recipient (cannot inject into a victim batch); a self-batch only moves the attacker's own funds; the nudge double-pay self-reverts (full-balance snapshot transfer underflows the drained balance) and the inner frame's forceApprove(minter,0) makes the outer loop's remaining mints revert; the minReward floor cannot be escaped. Recommendation: add OZ ReentrancyGuard regardless and make the refund credit a recorded amount instead of balanceOf(this).

evidence.strongest: Validated Tier-3 PoC workspace/phoenix-nft-staking/test/poc-L01-reentrancy.t.sol (4 cases, all pass against real source) per ledger L-01; corroborated this run by SLITHER-006, PATTERN-MR-001, and Tier-2 reentry-path tracing.

canonicalFindings.title: Uncapped caller-supplied count loop in batchMint
canonicalFindings.rootCause: for (uint256 i; i < count; ++i) nftMinter.mint(...) iterates a caller-supplied count with no upper bound and one external mint per iteration. Self-bounded: the caller pays each mint at the dispatcher's geometrically ramping price and bears their own gas; no shared/growing state, so no third-party DoS.
canonicalFindings.bestDescription: batchMint loops over a caller-supplied count with an external nftMinter.mint() per iteration and no max-count cap or pagination. The pattern matches the DB unbounded-loop template, but realistic impact is LOW: the loop touches no shared/growing array, the caller funds their own gas, and the dispatcher's ramping per-mint price makes a large count economically self-limiting. Only caller self-DoS, no cross-user griefing.

evidence.strongest: Static + pattern corroboration at HEAD 5f863d2; behavior unchanged from prior runs (ledger L-02).

canonicalFindings.title: Transient solvency-invariant window: topUp/setTargetAPY recompute the budget without a preceding pull(), over-stating budget while mintDebt > 0
canonicalFindings.rootCause: _recomputeSchedule sizes the budget on balance + dispatcherHook.mintDebt(), but topUp and setTargetAPY recompute WITHOUT first calling pull(). In the transient window where mintDebt > 0, the documented invariant 'Solvency (always): balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt' does not literally hold; it self-heals on the next _syncBudget/pullAndRefresh.
canonicalFindings.bestDescription: topUp and setTargetAPY call the schedule recompute without first pulling outstanding mintDebt, so during a window where dispatcherHook.mintDebt() > 0 the budget is over-stated by exactly the un-pulled mintDebt and the 'balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt' solvency invariant is transiently violated. Tier-3 confirmed the over-statement is precisely mintDebt and is restored by the next pullAndRefresh/_syncBudget. The only residual impact is a minor, recoverable claim-DoS tail IF the hook is rotated or breaks during that exact window. Best treated as a doc-precision fix (qualify the invariant as eventually-consistent) plus an optional pull() before recompute.

evidence.strongest: Tier-3 confirmation that the transient over-statement equals mintDebt and is restored by pullAndRefresh.

canonicalFindings.consolidationNote: Single root cause across two source agents (same transient-window observation). NEW — not in ledger. Low/informational. Distinct from DEDUP-006 (this is a code transient-state window; that is stale prose in docs).

canonicalFindings.title: Documentation drift: runway/design docs describe stale reward models (TOTAL-SUPPLY T-model and 540-day fixed window) vs shipped TOTAL-STAKED (M-03)
canonicalFindings.rootCause: docs/runway-dynamics-and-apy-as-policy.md still calls the TOTAL-SUPPLY T model the 'current spec' while shipped code + CLAUDE.md use TOTAL-STAKED (M-03); docs/design.md is fully stale (540-day fixed-window model). An owner tuning APY off the doc's runway tables can mis-size runway.

locations.role: labels stale TOTAL-SUPPLY T-model as current spec

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: The runway documentation is out of sync with shipped behavior: runway-dynamics-and-apy-as-policy.md presents the TOTAL-SUPPLY T model as the current spec, but the code and submodule CLAUDE.md size emission on TOTAL-STAKED post-M-03; design.md describes an entirely superseded 540-day fixed-window model. Because the owner is expected to tune targetAPY against the doc's runway tables, the drift is a non-obvious footgun: APY chosen from stale tables can mis-size the real runway. Fix is documentation (mark design.md superseded; update the runway doc to the TOTAL-STAKED/variable-runway model).

nudgeAmount relies on the 0 default (0 = no nudge) and loop counter i defaults to 0 — idiomatic Solidity, benign.

block.timestamp usage in the accrual/runway math is inherent to a time-driven reward schedule; kept by-design per time-driven-protocol policy. Several (015/016/017) are call-graph artifacts with no direct timestamp dependence.

latestPrice = price.mulDiv(...) then S = totalStaked * latestPrice floors conservatively-for-protocol; error bound ~totalStaked wei vs S~1e27 is negligible; explicitly in the project knownIssues as intentional (warns against flipping to ceiling). Accepted known design, not a live defect.
